text: Critical agent endpoints that create, plan, execute, pause, resume, cancel agent runs, or handle chat completions must require strict token authentication via the require_strict_operator_access dependency. The 01 auth front hardened seven critical endpoints: POST /v2/chat/agent, POST /v2/agent/runs, POST /v2/agent/runs/{run_id}/plan, execute, pause, resume, cancel, and POST /v1/chat/completions. Unauthenticated requests receive 403 Forbidden with no localhost bypass allowed. Valid BRAIN_ADMIN_TOKEN requests return 200 OK. Read-only mode gates remain active and block write tools even for authenticated requests. Fourteen auth endpoint tests passed, alongside memory hygiene, 08F batch promotion, 08B promotion tool, semantic retrieval hygiene, and FAISS rebuild hydration tests. Operator access now requires explicit token validation on every protected call.
summary: Auth hardening requires strict token auth on critical agent endpoints

text: Runtime semantic memory and FAISS vector indexes must remain local and untracked by Git to prevent repository bloat and accidental exposure of mutable runtime state. The memory git hygiene front successfully untracked semantic_memory.jsonl, semantic_memory_faiss.index, semantic_memory_faiss_ids.json, promotion_audit.jsonl, autonomous_journal.jsonl, and rollback_snapshots while preserving all 1756 JSONL records and 1747 FAISS vectors from prior 08F promotions. The .gitignore was updated to block memory semantic files, autonomous journal, rollback snapshots, audit CSVs, and batch promotion progress artifacts. A guard script at scripts/git_hygiene/check_no_sensitive_paths_staged.py now inspects staged files and fails if any sensitive runtime path is added, modified, or copied. All regression tests passed: memory git hygiene, 08F batch promotion, 08B promotion tool, semantic retrieval hygiene, and FAISS rebuild hydration. Local backups were created and hash-verified before untracking.
summary: Runtime memory must be local and untracked, not committed

text: Promotion batches must deduplicate by exact normalized text content, not only by candidate_id, because unique identifiers can still represent duplicate semantic content. The 08F front demonstrated that thirty-six submitted entries reduced to only twenty-eight unique candidate IDs and further to twenty-four unique normalized texts after deduplication. Failing to deduplicate by text allows redundant canonical memory entries that bloat the index, increase retrieval noise, and degrade semantic integrity. The deduplication pipeline normalizes whitespace and case before comparing text bodies, ensuring truly unique lessons are promoted while duplicates are silently skipped. All twenty-four promoted IDs were verified present in both JSONL and FAISS indexes, text hashes were confirmed unique, and retrieval samples passed. This practice preserves vector index quality and prevents semantic drift from repeated near-identical entries.
summary: Promotion batches must deduplicate by normalized text, not just candidate ID
